mainTopic: Oil and frankincense on the מנחת חוטא: what disqualifies it, ground לבונה, and the rule of דחויין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate: should מנחת כהנים or שתי הלחם be included with the עומר in needing oil and frankincense? The word נפש shows that the rule covers a private person's offering, so מנחת כהנים is the one included. Then a new משנה teaches that putting oil or לבונה on a מנחת חוטא is two separate prohibitions. Oil ruins the offering, but לבונה can be picked off. A ברייתא learns this from the פסוק and explains it: oil soaks in and cannot be removed, while לבונה can be gathered off. רבה בר רב הונא asks about ground לבונה, and a ברייתא shows that the מנחה is not fit until the לבונה is removed. The גמרא then asks why bad intent still counts on such a מנחה. אביי, רבא and רב אשי each answer, and רב אדא favors רב אשי: a problem you can fix yourself does not make an offering דחוי. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן's rules about how much oil or לבונה disqualifies the מנחה, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שתי הלחם share more features with the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that שתי הלחם should be the one included with the עומר, because they share eleven features. That is more than the features shared by מנחת כהנים and the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should have included the two loaves instead! They match the עומר in many ways: both are communal, obligatory, can be brought in impurity, are eaten, are subject to פיגול, are brought on שבת, permit something, are waved, come from ארץ ישראל, have a fixed time, and come from the new crop. These similarities are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier choice to include מנחת כהנים with the עומר. It lists eleven ways שתי הלחם is more like the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reasoning picked מנחת כהנים because it is similar to the עומר. But if similarity is the test, שתי הלחם wins, since it shares eleven features with the עומר. That is more than the features shared by מנחת כהנים. So the earlier choice seems to be the wrong one.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות for the whole community
To include in a rule from the extra words of a פסוק
The community, as opposed to a private individual
פיגול: an offering made invalid by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Waving: the offering is moved back and forth before ה'
They are more numerous

steps.confusionAlert: The list is in shorthand, one word for each shared feature. Each word names a way both שתי הלחם and the עומר are alike, and a way מנחת כהנים is different.

phrases.english: He should have included the two loaves,
phrases.notes: He means the extra word in the פסוק should have included the שתי הלחם instead of a מנחת כהנים.

phrases.english: since they are both: communal, obligatory,
brought in impurity, and eaten,
phrases.notes: Both can be brought even when the community is impure, and the כהנים eat them. A מנחת כהנים is burned completely.

phrases.english: subject to piggul, brought on Shabbat,
they permit something, they are waved, they come from the Land,
phrases.notes: The עומר permits eating the new crop, and שתי הלחם permits bringing מנחות from the new crop.

phrases.english: at a fixed time, from the new crop,
and these similarities are more numerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier decision, from before this section, to include מנחת כהנים based on its similarity to the עומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of מנחת כהנים as the מנחה included with the עומר for oil and frankincense.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If similarity decides, שתי הלחם shares eleven features with the עומר. That outnumbers the features shared by מנחת כהנים, so שתי הלחם should be included instead.

steps.title: The word 'נפש' points to an individual's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is still more logical to include מנחת כהנים, because the פסוק uses the word נפש, 'a person.' That word points to an individual's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to include מנחת כהנים, because the פסוק says 'נפש', a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its original choice of מנחת כהנים. It points to the word נפש in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting similarities is not the deciding factor here. The word נפש means one person, so the פסוק is talking about private offerings. מנחת כהנים is brought by an individual כהן, while שתי הלחם is a communal offering. So it cannot be the one the פסוק includes, no matter how many other features it shares.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it is more logical
Literally 'a soul'; here it means one individual person

steps.whatToRemember: Even though שתי הלחם has more points of similarity to the עומר, the word נפש limits the rule to individual offerings. So מנחת כהנים, not שתי הלחם, is the one included.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a word in the פסוק can outweigh a count of similarities when deciding what a rule includes.

phrases.english: It stands to reason, because the verse says 'a person.'
phrases.notes: The word נפש in the פסוק about מנחות means a single person. So it fits a private offering like מנחת כהנים, not a communal one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 and keeps the original choice of מנחת כהנים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word in the פסוק outweighs counting similarities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the offering with the most similarities, שתי הלחם, should be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word נפש limits the rule to individual offerings. So מנחת כהנים is included and שתי הלחם is not.

steps.title: Separate punishment for oil and frankincense, and which one ruins the offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that oil and frankincense are two separate prohibitions. Oil disqualifies the מנחת חוטא, but frankincense can be gathered off it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person is punished for the oil by itself and for the frankincense by itself. If he put oil on the offering, it is disqualified. If he put frankincense on it, he should pick the frankincense off.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the rules for someone who wrongly puts oil or frankincense on the מנחת חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil and frankincense are two different לאווין, so doing both brings two sets of מלקות. The results are different, though. Oil soaks into the flour and ruins the offering. Frankincense sits on top, so it can be removed and the offering is saved.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering of a poor sinner, brought without oil or frankincense
Frankincense
By itself, as a separate count
He disqualified it
He should gather it up (pick it off)

steps.confusionAlert: Both oil and frankincense are forbidden. The difference is only in the result: oil ruins the offering, while frankincense can be picked off and the offering is still fine.

phrases.english: MISHNA
And he is liable for the oil by itself,
phrases.notes: This picks up the earlier משנה about putting oil or frankincense on the sinner's offering or the סוטה's offering.

phrases.english: and he is liable for frankincense by itself.
If he put oil on it, he has disqualified it;
if frankincense, he should gather it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves away from the עומר discussion in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil and frankincense are separate prohibitions. Oil disqualifies the offering, and frankincense is simply removed.

steps.title: Limits of the prohibition: the leftovers, and a vessel resting on a vessel
steps.stepSummary: Oil put on the leftovers is not a violation. Oil in a separate vessel set on top does not disqualify the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put oil on its leftovers, he does not break the prohibition. If he put a vessel on top of a vessel, he did not disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two limits to the rules it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition applies only before the קמיצה. Once the כהן has taken out the handful, the leftovers are no longer included. Also, the oil must actually touch the offering. A separate vessel of oil sitting above it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Its leftovers, what remains after the handful (קמיצה) is taken out
A negative commandment (prohibition)
A vessel on top of a vessel

phrases.english: If he put oil on its leftovers,
he does not violate a prohibition;
if he put a vessel on top of a vessel,
phrases.notes: A vessel with oil set on top of the vessel holding the offering.

phrases.english: he did not disqualify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits on the rules of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no violation on the leftovers, and no disqualification when the oil is in a separate vessel on top.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the verse teaches that oil disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'he shall place no oil upon it' that oil is forbidden and, if put on, disqualifies the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: 'He shall place no oil upon it.' And if he did place it, he disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule that oil ruins the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא starts with the oil half of the פסוק. It says the ban on oil is not just a prohibition. Breaking it also makes the offering invalid. This sets up the next question: does frankincense work the same way?

keyTerms.meaning: He shall place no oil upon it (ויקרא 5:11)
He disqualified it

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Rabbis taught:
"He shall place no oil upon it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11

phrases.english: and if he placed it, he disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יָשִׂים עָלֶיהָ שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for step 3's rule that oil disqualifies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil on the מנחת חוטא disqualifies it.

steps.title: Maybe frankincense also disqualifies?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that frankincense might disqualify the offering just like oil does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: he may not put frankincense on it, and if he did, he disqualified it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible first thought. It is setting up the next step, where the פסוק will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil and frankincense appear side by side in the same פסוק. So you might assume they have the same result, and frankincense also ruins the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (introduces a first assumption)

phrases.english: One might think: he may not put frankincense on it,
and if he put it, he disqualified it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether step 5's rule for oil also applies to frankincense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does frankincense disqualify the offering like oil does?

steps.title: 'For it is a sin offering': frankincense does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The words 'for it is a sin offering' teach that the offering stays valid even with frankincense on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For it is a sin offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the end of the פסוק that frankincense does not ruin the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it a חטאת even after it mentions frankincense. This shows the offering keeps its status, so the frankincense is just picked off. This is the source for the משנה's word יִלְקְטֶנָּה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the answer from a פסוק)
For it is a sin offering

phrases.english: The verse states: "For it is a sin offering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11. Even with frankincense on it, it is still called a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Frankincense does not disqualify, because it is still a חטאת.

steps.title: Then maybe oil also does not disqualify?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'for it is a sin offering' should also save the offering when oil is put on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the same is true even of oil?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new worry. It is setting up the last step, where the פסוק will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כִּי חַטָּאת come after both oil and frankincense in the פסוק. So maybe they keep the offering valid in both cases. That would cancel what step 5 taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Even with oil

phrases.english: One might think: even with oil?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes step 7's reading onto oil too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'for it is a sin offering' also keep the offering valid when oil is put on it?

steps.title: The word 'it' limits the rule: oil still disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The word הִיא limits the rule. Only with frankincense does it stay a valid חטאת, not with oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'It is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by learning from the extra word הִיא that oil still ruins the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הִיא, 'it is', narrows the rule. It stays a חטאת only in the frankincense case. So both rules of the משנה now have a source: oil disqualifies, and frankincense is picked off.

keyTerms.meaning: It (is), a limiting word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Oil on a מנחת חוטא ruins it (לֹא יָשִׂים). Frankincense does not ruin it, because it is still a חטאת. The word הִיא keeps oil out of that leniency.

phrases.english: The verse states: "It is."
phrases.notes: The full phrase is 'for it is a sin offering.' The word 'it' narrows the rule to frankincense only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 and confirms step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The word הִיא limits the leniency to frankincense, so oil still disqualifies.

steps.title: Why make oil the disqualifier and not frankincense?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason we have to say oil disqualifies the מנחה while לבונה leaves it valid, rather than the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you disqualify with oil and validate with frankincense?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading from Steps 7–9. It asks why oil should be the one that ruins the offering and לבונה the one that does not, and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, the word הִיא was used to limit the rule so that only לבונה keeps the offering valid. But the word itself does not say which item it limits. So the ברייתא asks why we chose to apply it this way and not the reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? A request for the reason behind a choice between two possible readings
To disqualify (make the offering invalid)
To make valid / keep it fit
Frankincense

phrases.english: And what did you see
phrases.notes: In other words: what reason do you have to read it this way?

phrases.english: to disqualify with oil
and to validate with frankincense?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לִפְסוֹל בַּשֶּׁמֶן וּלְהַכְשִׁיר בַּלְּבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the direction of the limitation drawn from הִיא in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason justifies applying the disqualification to oil and the validity to לבונה, rather than the reverse?

steps.title: Oil cannot be removed, frankincense can
steps.stepSummary: Oil disqualifies because once it is on the flour it cannot be taken out. לבונה does not disqualify because it can be picked off.
steps.simpleTranslation: I disqualify with oil, since it is impossible to gather it up. And I validate with frankincense, since it is possible to gather it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. Oil soaks into the flour and cannot be removed, so it ruins the offering. לבונה sits on top and can be picked off, so the offering stays valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives a logical reason for the reading. If the forbidden item can be removed, the offering can go back to how it was. If it cannot be removed, the offering is changed for good, so it makes sense that oil is the disqualifier.

keyTerms.meaning: I disqualify
It is impossible
To gather it up / pick it out
I validate

steps.whyThisMatters: The reason 'can it be gathered' becomes the basis for the dilemma about ground frankincense in the next step.

phrases.english: I disqualify with oil,
since it is impossible to gather it up,
and I validate with frankincense,
since it is possible to gather it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹסֵל אֲנִי בַּשֶּׁמֶן, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְלׇקְטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 with a logical reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Oil cannot be removed once added, but לבונה can be gathered off, so oil disqualifies and לבונה does not.

steps.title: What about ground-up frankincense?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא asks רבי יוחנן about powdered לבונה. It cannot be gathered like oil, yet it does not soak in like oil. Which reason decides?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא asked רבי יוחנן: If one placed ground frankincense on it, what is the law? Is the reason because it can be gathered, and this cannot be gathered? Or perhaps the reason is because it is not absorbed, and this too is not absorbed?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבה בר רב הונא asks about powdered לבונה placed on the מנחה, since it falls between the two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular לבונה has two features: it can be picked off, and it does not soak into the flour. Ground לבונה keeps only the second feature. So the question is which feature is the real reason the offering stays valid. If it is 'can be gathered,' the offering is disqualified. If it is 'not absorbed,' it stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked / raised a dilemma (a בְּעָיָא, a question where both sides are reasonable)
Ground into powder
What is the law?
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the question)
It is absorbed / soaks in

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna asked of Rabbi Yochanan:
If he placed ground frankincense on it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'On it' means on the sinner's מנחה.

phrases.english: Is it because it is possible to gather it,
and this one cannot be gathered?
Or perhaps it is because it is not absorbed,
and this one too is not absorbed?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new dilemma on the reason given in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason לבונה does not disqualify that it can be gathered, or that it is not absorbed? This decides the law for ground לבונה.

steps.title: Proof from 'he should gather it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from the משנה, which says the לבונה should be gathered off. That suggests gathering is the key, so ground לבונה would disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And the frankincense, he should gather it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the question with the משנה's words, which say that if לבונה was put on, it should be gathered off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה mentions only gathering, it looks like the offering is valid only when the לבונה can be gathered. Ground לבונה cannot be gathered, so by this proof it would disqualify the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: He should gather it up
The meal offering brought by a sinner (the case under discussion)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And frankincense, he should gather it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve the dilemma of Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the reason is 'it can be gathered,' so ground לבונה disqualifies.

steps.title: The משנה may be giving two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside. The משנה may mean that לבונה is fine for one main reason (it does not soak in), and also because it can be gathered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it states one reason and another: one, that it is not absorbed; and another, he should gather it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe the משנה is giving a second, extra reason, and the main reason is that לבונה does not soak in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'not absorbed' is enough by itself, mentioning gathering does not show that gathering is required. Ground לבונה, which is still not absorbed, could then be valid. So the proof does not settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: It says one reason and adds another
Perhaps (introducing a pushback on a proof)

steps.whatToRemember: Regular לבונה has two features: it does not soak in, and it can be gathered. The משנה's word 'gather' does not prove which feature matters, so this proof fails. Step 18 brings the ברייתא that settles the question.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say ground לבונה is valid. It only shows the proof from the משנה is not strong enough.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is stating one reason and another:
one, that it is not absorbed,
and another, he should gather it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the dilemma.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes gathering is the only reason, but the משנה may be adding gathering as a second reason next to 'not absorbed.'

steps.title: Another try: the ברייתא says לבונה can be gathered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the ברייתא's wording 'since it is possible to gather it' that gathering is the deciding reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'I declare it valid with לבונה, since it is possible to gather it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof for רבה בר רב הונא's question, this time from the words of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only one reason for why לבונה does not disqualify: it can be gathered off. If that is the whole reason, then ground לבונה, which cannot be gathered, should disqualify the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: I declare it valid (kosher)
to gather it up / pick it off

phrases.english: Come and hear:
I declare it valid with frankincense,
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא we saw in steps 10–11. Now the גמרא looks closely at its exact wording.

phrases.english: since it is possible to gather it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַכְשִׁיר אֲנִי בַּלְּבוֹנָה, שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְלוֹקְטָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof attempt after the first proof from the משנה was pushed aside in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That gathering, and not soaking in, is what decides. So ground לבונה would disqualify.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own stated reason: 'since it is possible to gather it.'

steps.title: Again: one reason plus an extra one
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא may also be giving an extra reason on top of the main one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, he is saying one reason and then another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside this proof the same way it pushed aside the proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main reason may still be that לבונה does not soak in. 'It can be gathered' could be an extra, second reason. So the wording does not prove that gathering alone decides.

keyTerms.meaning: one reason, and another besides: giving an extra reason on top of the main one

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: Here too means just like the answer to the משנה in step 14.

phrases.english: he is saying one reason and another.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 15 using the same approach as step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stated reason may be a secondary reason, not the only one.

steps.title: So what is the final answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבה בר רב הונא's question was finally decided.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of this question?
steps.whatsHappening: Both proofs failed, so the גמרא asks for the final answer. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a transition. The question about ground לבונה is still open, and the גמרא now looks for a source that will really settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: what was concluded about it? (a request for the final resolution)

phrases.english: What came of it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבה בר רב הונא's question about ground לבונה from step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed proofs, the גמרא asks for the final resolution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How was רבה בר רב הונא's question about ground לבונה settled?

steps.title: A ברייתא about intent before and after gathering the לבונה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a ברייתא. Improper intent before the לבונה is gathered cannot make the מנחה פיגול. After gathering, it can. So the מנחה is not fit until the לבונה is removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A ברייתא teaches: if someone put לבונה on a sinner's מנחה or on the מנחה of a סוטה, he gathers off the לבונה and it is valid. If, before he gathered the לבונה, the כהן had intent to do it beyond its time or outside its place, it is disqualified, but there is no כרת. If he had the intent after gathering the לבונה: outside its place, it is disqualified with no כרת; beyond its time, it is פיגול and one is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question with a ברייתא. It shows that the מנחה only becomes a proper offering once the לבונה is gathered off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, intent to eat an offering beyond its time makes it פיגול, which carries כרת. Here, before the לבונה is gathered, the same intent gives no כרת. That means the מנחה is not yet a fit offering while the לבונה sits on it. So what fixes it is gathering, and ground לבונה, which cannot be gathered, would disqualify the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: the sinner's מנחה, brought by a poor person. It must have no oil and no לבונה.
the 'meal offering of jealousy' brought by a סוטה. It also has no oil and no לבונה.
beyond its time: intent to offer or eat it after the allowed time
outside its place: intent to offer or eat it outside the allowed area
an offering made disgusting by intent to eat it beyond its time. Eating it carries כרת.
spiritual cutting off, a severe heavenly punishment

steps.whatToRemember: While the לבונה is still on it, the מנחה is not a fit offering, since intent cannot make it פיגול. Gathering the לבונה is what makes it fit. So gathering is the key reason.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No כרת' here does not mean the case is lighter or better. It means the מנחה was not a proper offering at that moment, so the special פיגול punishment cannot apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles רבה בר רב הונא's question: ground לבונה, which cannot be gathered, would disqualify the מנחה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is taught in a baraita:
A sinner's meal offering or a meal offering of jealousy
phrases.notes: The 'meal offering of jealousy' is the one brought by a סוטה. Neither offering is supposed to have לבונה.

phrases.english: on which one put frankincense –
he gathers off the frankincense, and it is valid.
And if, before he gathered its frankincense,
he had intent about it,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן had a wrong intention while doing the service, about when or where it would be offered or eaten.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ בֵּין חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ –
phrases.english: whether beyond its time or outside its place –
it is disqualified, and there is no karet for it.
And if, after he gathered its frankincense,
he has intent about it outside its place –
it is disqualified, and there is no karet.
Beyond its time –
it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it.
phrases.notes: This is the normal rule for a fit offering. The contrast with line 9 is the whole proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with a new ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Before the לבונה is gathered, the מנחה is not a fit offering, so פיגול does not apply. Gathering is what makes it fit, so ground לבונה would disqualify.

steps.title: Challenge: if it is unfit, why does intent matter at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the מנחה is unfit while the לבונה is on it, it should be like a מנחה with oil poured on from a jug: fully rejected. So why does the ברייתא say improper intent disqualifies it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it be like a מנחה with oil poured from a jug. Why does the ברייתא say intent disqualifies it? It is already rejected!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא just quoted. It finds a problem inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the מנחה as unfit before the לבונה is gathered. If so, it is like a מנחה with oil on it, which is simply rejected. Something already rejected should not be 'disqualified' by bad intent, because there is nothing left to disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: a jug or flask, here a flask of oil
intent, the כהן's thought during the service
rejected, already pushed out of being a valid offering

phrases.english: But let it be like a jug,
phrases.notes: He means a sinner's מנחה with oil poured on it from a jug. That one is disqualified, as we learned in steps 10–11.

phrases.english: and why does it become disqualified through intent?
It is already rejected!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks a detail of the ברייתא brought in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that intent before gathering 'disqualifies' the מנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the לבונה makes the מנחה unfit, like oil does, the מנחה is already rejected. Intent should have no effect on something already rejected.

steps.title: אביי: The תורה still calls it a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תורה calls this מנחה a חטאת even while the לבונה is on it, so improper intent affects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Merciful One calls it a 'sin offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer to the question from step 19. Even while the לבונה is on it, the תורה calls this מנחה a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that an unfit מנחה should be fully rejected, so improper intent should not matter. אביי answers that the פסוק still gives it the name חטאת. Because it keeps the status of a real offering, improper intent can still disqualify it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering; here it means the מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא, the meal offering of a sinner
The Merciful One, a name the גמרא uses for God as the author of the תורה

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Merciful One calls it "a sin offering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11. The point is that it is called a sin offering even while it is not yet fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural status: the פסוק's name for the offering keeps it significant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unfit מנחה is fully rejected, so improper intent has no effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the תורה calls it a חטאת even in this state, improper intent does affect it.

steps.title: רבא: The ברייתא follows חנן המצרי
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא follows חנן המצרי, who holds that a temporarily unfit offering is not permanently rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whose view is this? It is חנן המצרי, who does not hold of rejection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different answer. He says the ברייתא follows one particular תנא, חנן המצרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 19 assumed the rule of דחויין: once an offering becomes unfit, it stays rejected for good. רבא answers that חנן המצרי does not accept that rule. So according to him, the מנחה is not rejected while the לבונה is on it, and improper intent still matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? (a question asking which תנא a source follows)
Rejection: the rule that an offering that became unfit is rejected permanently

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whose opinion is this?
It is Chanan the Egyptian,
who does not hold of rejection.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי? חָנָן הַמִּצְרִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds that an unfit offering is permanently rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows חנן המצרי, who does not hold of דחויין.

steps.title: Source showing חנן המצרי rejects the rule of דחויין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that חנן המצרי lets a new goat be paired with an already-slaughtered יום כיפור goat, so the slaughtered goat is not rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: חנן המצרי says: Even if the blood is already in the cup, one brings a partner goat without a lottery and pairs it with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that חנן המצרי really does not hold of דחויין. This backs up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור there are two goats, one for ה׳ and one sent to עזאזל, and a lottery decides which is which. If the sent-away goat is lost after the other goat's blood is already collected, you might expect the blood to be rejected. חנן המצרי says you simply bring a new partner goat with no new lottery, so nothing becomes permanently rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood in the cup: the blood was already collected in a vessel after slaughter
The lottery that assigns the two יום כיפור goats
Pairs, matches up as partner

phrases.english: As it is taught: Chanan the Egyptian says:
Even if the blood is in the cup,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the יום כיפור goat for ה׳, in a case where its partner goat, the one to be sent away, was lost.

phrases.english: one brings its partner without a lottery
and pairs it with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's claim about חנן המצרי.
steps.raayaObject: That חנן המצרי does not hold of דחויין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the יום כיפור goats: even with the blood already in the cup, a new partner goat is brought and paired.

steps.title: רב אשי: What you can fix yourself is not rejected
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that since the כהן can remove the לבונה himself, the מנחה is not considered rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Anything that is in one's own power to fix is not considered rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. He says an offering is only rejected when the problem is out of your hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the only thing stopping the מנחה is the לבונה on top, and the כהן can gather it off whenever he wants. Since fixing it is fully in his control, the מנחה never counts as rejected. So improper intent can still disqualify it, even according to those who hold of דחויין.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that is in his hand, meaning anything he can fix himself
Rejected, permanently disqualified as an offering

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Anything that is in his hand
phrases.notes: He means here that the כהן can just gather off the לבונה himself.

phrases.english: is not rejected.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about דחויין: a temporary problem the person can solve on his own does not count as rejection.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of step 19, different from those of אביי and רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the limits of דחוי: something within one's control does not count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any temporary unfitness makes the מנחה rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since removing the לבונה is in the כהן's hands, the מנחה is not rejected, so improper intent still matters.

steps.title: רב אדא: רב אשי's answer makes the most sense
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא says רב אשי's answer is the most reasonable, and starts his argument: the one known to hold of דחויין is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said: It stands to reason like רב אשי. For whom have you heard who holds of rejection? It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא picks a side among the three answers and supports רב אשי. He starts by asking who is the known source for the rule of דחויין, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא's argument is built on identifying who holds of דחויין, and he names רבי יהודה. The source for רבי יהודה's view comes in the next step. Step 26 completes his reasoning for why this favors רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes more sense
In line with him, like his view

phrases.english: Rav Adda said:
It stands to reason in line with Rav Ashi,
for whom have you heard
who holds of rejection?
It is Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא: כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Weighs the answers given so far and sides with רב אשי (step 23).
steps.raayaObject: That רב אשי's answer is the most reasonable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the known holder of דחויין is רבי יהודה (source given in the next step).

steps.title: רבי יהודה's משנה about the יום כיפור goats
steps.stepSummary: The משנה shows that רבי יהודה holds of דחויין: if one יום כיפור goat is lost to the service, its partner is rejected too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: And רבי יהודה also said: If the blood spilled, the sent-away goat must die. If the sent-away goat died, the blood must be spilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה proving that רבי יהודה holds of דחויין. This is the source for רב אדא's claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two יום כיפור goats work as a pair. רבי יהודה says that if either one is lost, the other is rejected for good: the sent-away goat is left to die, or the blood is poured out. This is the opposite of חנן המצרי, who lets you bring a new partner.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood spilled before it was sprinkled
The goat that is sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two goats. 'The blood' belongs to the goat offered to ה׳, while 'the sent-away goat' is the one for עזאזל.

phrases.english: as we learned: And Rabbi Yehuda also said:
If the blood spilled, the sent-away goat must die;
if the sent-away goat died, the blood must be spilled.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers for why improper intent works on a מנחה with its לבונה still on it. אביי: it is still called a חטאת. רבא: the ברייתא follows חנן המצרי, who does not hold of דחויין. רב אשי: what is in your hands to fix is not rejected. רב אדא favors רב אשי, noting that רבי יהודה is the one who holds of דחויין.
steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם יָמוּת הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב אדא's claim that רבי יהודה holds of דחויין.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds of דחויין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (יומא) about the יום כיפור goats: if one is lost, its partner is rejected.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees a fixable problem does not reject an offering
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא completes his proof: when the כהן can fix the problem himself, even רבי יהודה does not treat the offering as rejected. His proof is the cup of mixed blood thrown at the base of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where the fix is in his own hands, it is taught: רבי יהודה says the כהן would fill a cup from the mixed blood on the floor and throw it once against the base of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא finishes his argument for רב אשי. He shows that רבי יהודה, who usually holds of דחויין, agrees there is no rejection when the כהן can fix things himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, רבי יהודה held that a lost goat makes its partner rejected, because nobody could fix that. Here the spilled blood can be fixed by scooping up the mixed blood and throwing it, so nothing is rejected. So even רבי יהודה, the one תנא who holds of דחויין, agrees with רב אשי's rule. That means the ברייתא about the לבונה works for everyone, and there is no need for רבא's answer that it follows only חנן המצרי.

keyTerms.meaning: In his hand: the problem is something the person can fix himself
The mixed blood of many offerings that spilled together on the floor
Throwing the blood onto the מזבח
The base of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי יהודה, who holds of דחויין, agrees that a problem the כהן can fix himself does not make the offering rejected. This is why רב אדא says רב אשי's answer is the best one.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה changed his mind about דחויין. He still holds of it. He only says it does not apply when the fix is in the כהן's own hands.

phrases.english: And yet, where it is in his power to fix,
it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He would fill a cup
from the mixed blood,
phrases.notes: This is the blood of many offerings that spilled together on the floor. The cup covers any offering whose own blood was lost.

phrases.english: and throw it in one throwing
against the base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 25: there the problem could not be fixed, so the partner was rejected; here it can be fixed, so nothing is rejected.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's answer that a מנחה is not rejected when the כהן can remove the לבונה himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה rules that the mixed blood is thrown at the base, so offerings with spilled blood are fixed

steps.title: Any amount of oil on a כזית of מנחה disqualifies it
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רבי יוחנן rules that even a tiny bit of oil placed on at least a כזית of a מנחת חוטא disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone put any amount of oil on a כזית of the מנחה, he disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement about the מנחת חוטא, which must not have oil on it. It sets the amounts for oil to disqualify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two measurements here. For the oil, there is no minimum: even a drop counts. For the מנחה, the oil must be on at least a כזית of flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Any tiny amount
The size of an olive, a basic halachic measurement
He disqualified it
The meal offering of a sinner, which may not have oil or לבונה

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he put any amount of oil
on top of an olive's size of meal offering,
phrases.notes: This is the מנחת חוטא, the poor sinner's offering, which must be brought without oil.

phrases.english: he disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נָתָן מַשֶּׁהוּ שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about oil on the מנחת חוטא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any amount of oil placed on at least a כזית of a מנחת חוטא disqualifies it.

steps.title: The פסוק's words teach both amounts for oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason. "לא ישים" teaches that any amount of oil counts, and "עליה" teaches that the מנחה must be a real measure, a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? "He shall not place": placing counts with any amount. "Upon it": only when there is a proper measure of the מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי יוחנן's two measurements come from, using two words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for placing oil (שימה) has no built-in amount, so any oil counts. The word "עליה" (on it) points to the מנחה itself, which must be a real-sized portion, a כזית, before it is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing, the word the פסוק uses for oil
Any amount at all
Upon it, meaning on the מנחה
A set measurement, here a כזית

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"He shall not place": placing, with any amount,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11

phrases.english: "upon it": only when there is a proper measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: Any oil disqualifies, but only on a כזית of מנחה

steps.title: A כזית of לבונה on any amount of מנחה disqualifies it
steps.stepSummary: A second ruling of רבי יוחנן: a כזית of לבונה placed on even a tiny bit of מנחה disqualifies it, which is the reverse of the oil rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone put a כזית of לבונה on any amount of מנחה, he disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a matching rule for לבונה. The measurements are flipped compared to the oil rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With oil, any amount of oil counts, but it needs a כזית of מנחה. With לבונה, it needs a כזית of לבונה, but any amount of מנחה counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, which may not be put on the מנחת חוטא
On top of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. Oil: tiny oil on a כזית of מנחה. לבונה: a כזית of לבונה on a tiny bit of מנחה.

phrases.english: And Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he put an olive's size of frankincense
on top of any amount of meal offering,
he disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נָתָן כְּזַיִת לְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling to step 27, with the measurements reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית of לבונה placed on any amount of a מנחת חוטא disqualifies it.

steps.title: "לא יתן" teaches that לבונה needs a real amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the reason: "לא יתן" means a real act of giving, which needs a כזית of לבונה. It then begins explaining "עליה", and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? "He shall not give" is written, which means only when there is a real giving. "Upon it"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a כזית of לבונה is needed. It starts to explain the word "עליה", and that explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק uses the word for giving (נתינה), which only counts with a real amount, a כזית. That is different from the oil, where the word was placing (שימה), which counts with any amount. The word "עליה" will now explain why any amount of מנחה is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not give, the פסוק's words about לבונה
Giving, which only counts with a real amount (a כזית)
It is written

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"He shall not give" is written,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11

phrases.english: meaning only when there is a real giving.
"Upon it":
phrases.notes: The sentence stops here and finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 29, contrasting "יתן" with "ישים" from step 28.
steps.raayaObject: A כזית of לבונה is needed to disqualify
